clinical_note: DISCHARGE SUMMARY: 58-year-old male admitted with acute substernal chest pressure radiating to left arm with diaphoresis and dyspnea on exertion. Cardiac troponin peaked at 0.82 ng/mL. ECG showed ST depression in V4-V6. Underwent successful PCI with drug-eluting stent (DES) to mid-LAD artery. Prescribed Aspirin 81mg, Clopidogrel 75mg, Atorvastatin 80mg, Metoprolol 25mg, and Sublingual nitroglycerin 0.4mg PRN. Follow-up cardiology clinic in 2 weeks. Specific cardiologist name not designated in note.

CLINICAL ENCOUNTER NOTE: 34-year-old female presenting with 4-day history of escalating severe right-sided pulsatile cephalalgia preceded by scintillating scotomas and transient homonymous hemianopsia with photophobia and nausea. Brain MRI with gadolinium was unremarkable. Diagnosis: Intractable episodic migraine with typical visual aura. Plan: Sumatriptan 50mg at onset, Ondansetron 4mg ODT PRN, Topiramate 25mg nightly titration. Discontinue daily combined OTC analgesics. Follow up neurology clinic in 6 weeks.

INPATIENT PROGRESS NOTE: 66-year-old female presenting with 5-day history of progressive dyspnea, chills, nocturnal diaphoresis, and productive cough with purulent greenish sputum. History of COPD. SpO2 89% ambient air. Leukocytosis WBC 15.4k. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe alveolar consolidation with air bronchograms. Diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), acute exacerbation of COPD. Plan: Ceftriaxone 1g IV daily, Azithromycin 500mg IV daily, Duoneb nebulizer, Prednisone 40mg daily for 5 days. Repeat CXR before discharge. Outpatient antibiotic step-down pending final culture.

ED CONSULT NOTE: 45-year-old male with poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus presenting with polyuria, polydipsia, fatigue, and abdominal discomfort. Point-of-care blood glucose 385 mg/dL, serum beta-hydroxybutyrate 3.8 mmol/L, arterial pH 7.28, anion gap 18 mEq/L consistent with mild diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Initiated aggressive IV normal saline hydration and continuous regular insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr. Dextrose 5% added when glucose reached 240 mg/dL. Transition to subcutaneous Basaglar 24 units glargine daily and Humalog 6 units TID with meals. HbA1c pending from admission lab.

OUTPATIENT CLINIC NOTE: 52-year-old female presenting with 3-day history of steady left lower quadrant (LLQ) abdominal pain, low-grade pyrexia (37.9 C), and constipation. Abdominal CT with oral/IV contrast demonstrates focal colonic wall thickening and pericolonic fat stranding in the sigmoid colon without abscess or free intraperitoneal air. Diagnosis: Uncomplicated acute sigmoid diverticulitis. Commenced on oral Ciprofloxacin 500mg BID and Metronidazole 500mg TID for 10-day course with clear liquid diet progression. Follow-up colonoscopy recommended in 6 to 8 weeks after acute inflammation resolves.
